summary: This component renders a decorative button that scrolls the page back to the top when clicked. It only shows the button once you've scrolled down more than 300 pixels, and plays a brief animation when you click it. The button uses an image of a meerkat and includes proper accessibility labels for screen readers.

explanations.12: This checks how far down the page you've scrolled (window.scrollY) and only enables the button if you're past 300 pixels.
explanations.13: We attach a listener to the scroll event so that toggleVisibility runs whenever the user scrolls; the passive flag tells the browser it's safe to optimize.
explanations.14: When the component unmounts or dependencies change, we clean up by removing the scroll listener to prevent memory leaks.
explanations.18: We set fly to true to trigger a CSS animation class, making the button visually animate as it scrolls.
explanations.21: After 800 milliseconds (the duration of the animation), we turn off the fly animation so it doesn't loop.
explanations.27: clsx combines multiple class names conditionally—the button gets the 'show' class when visible and the 'fly' class when animating.
explanations.29: The aria-label makes the button accessible to screen readers; translate() provides the text in the user's language.
